podcast.body: After Soundgarden broke up in 1997, Chris Cornell had a backlog of material and began working on his solo debut in 1998. He relied on Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider of the band Eleven to help produce the record. Despite receiving good reviews, the album was a sales disappointment. "Chris reliant on both of them to help produce his debut solo record Euphoria Morning, which came out in 1999."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released on September 21, 1999, this album was put together over approximately 18 months with the assistance of friends from the band 11. It was recognized as a rock record, distinct from the "slab of sludge metal" characteristic of Soundgarden, instead featuring a more mature sound with textures previously unheard in his work with his former band. The album received critical acclaim. "Then on September 21st, 1999, Chris released a record called Euphoria Morning."
